item.title: Xpeng Vice Chairman Reveals: IRON Robot Price Comparable to Electric Cars, Earliest Launch in Q2 Next Year
item.description: Gu Hongdi, Vice Chairman of XPeng, revealed that the price of the IRON humanoid robot will be set with reference to electric vehicle prices and may be close to the median price of electric vehicles. XPeng's current models are priced between 119,800 and 309,800 yuan. IRON is expected to go on sale as early as the second quarter of 2027, with the goal of selling tens of thousands of units that year. Xingxing Wang, founder of Unitree Robotics, predicts that in the next 5 to 10 years, the annual production of robots in China is expected to exceed 20 million units, surpassing that of automobiles.
item.dc:creator: 华尔街见闻
item.content:encoded: The commercialization of humanoid robots is accelerating, and industry competition is now extending from technological R&D to product pricing, mass production capability, and practical application scenarios. On November 26, according to Bloomberg, Xpeng Vice Chairman Gu Hongdi revealed in an interview on Thursday that Xpeng IRON humanoid robot will be priced similarly to electric vehicles, possibly close to the median price of electric vehicles. The current price range for Xpeng's available models is approximately 119,800 to 309,800 yuan. IRON is planned to begin training as a retail assistant in the first quarter of 2027 and the earliest public sale may start in the second quarter. Gu Hongdi stated that Xpeng's goal is to sell tens of thousands of humanoid robots in 2027, viewing this year as a key phase for scaling up and commercialization. In addition to hardware sales, the company is optimistic about recurring revenue opportunities from software upgrades, training services, and data infrastructure for robots. This commercialization plan also reflects Xpeng’s desire to expand its robot business from a single hardware product to an integrated hardware and software model. In addition to IRON, Xpeng is pushing forward with other AI-related businesses such as autonomous driving and flying vehicles. The company announced this week that its first model designed specifically for Robotaxi is scheduled for release in 2027, following autonomous driving system trials in Guangzhou. From Hardware Sales to Recurring Revenue: Xpeng Expands Robot Business Model As Xpeng intensifies its focus on the robotics business, its core automotive operations are still in a phase of transformation and improved profitability. According to the third quarter earnings released by Xpeng this week, company revenue grew by 19% year-on-year, but profitability has yet to be achieved. While the automotive division continues with technological investments and adjustments to its product structure, new businesses such as robotics are expected to drive long-term growth prospects. Gu Hongdi mentioned that the company is addressing industry cost pressures through technology development, product adjustments, and model structure changes in order to improve profitability in its automotive business, while also promoting the commercial sustainability of its new ventures. For Xpeng, the robotics business is not only a new product line but also carries expectations for expanded growth opportunities. In terms of revenue models, hardware sales are just the first step. Software upgrades, training services, and data infrastructure are expected to become subsequent sources of income. However, whether this model is viable still depends on whether robots can be deployed in enough practical use cases and generate sustained customer demand. Will China’s Annual Robot Production Exceed 20 Million Units? While Xpeng is accelerating commercialization, expectations for the size of the robot market across the industry are also rising. On the same day, Unitree Robotics founder and chairman Wang Xingxing stated at the WISE2026 conference held in Beijing that, in the next 5 to 10 years, China’s annual robot production could exceed 20 million units, surpassing automobile production. This prediction equates the future scale of the robotics industry with that of the automotive sector. For automakers like Xpeng, experience gained in supply chain management, manufacturing, and cost control in the automotive space could become an advantage for their robotics operations. However, whether large-scale mass production of robots can be achieved still depends on manufacturing costs, technological maturity, and actual demand for applications. From Xpeng’s plan to sell tens of thousands of robots in 2027, to Wang Xingxing’s prediction that annual industry production could exceed 20 million units, the industry’s prospects are full of imagination, but true scale still requires market validation. Whether IRON can launch as planned and open up the consumer market will be a crucial test for the commercialization of Xpeng robots.
